title: Entropy-regulated canary with cost-safety and explainable fallbacks
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed cases where low-variance traffic (e.g., a narrow user cohort or highly similar request payloads) allowed harmful regressions to pass simple aggregate gates. This PR introduces an entropy-driven safety regulator for progressive rollouts that controls exposure by measuring request-feature diversity and coupling that signal with cost and explainability fallbacks. Summary: Adds an EntropyRegulator that computes a sliding-window entropy score over configurable request feature vectors (user cohort, intent hash, prompt fingerprint). The canary scheduler reduces traffic when entropy is below a threshold and stalls progress when cost-per-inference rises above a budgeted burn rate. If a canary pauses for safety, a lightweight explainable-model fallback is optionally activated for sampled traffic to surface interpretable decisions while the owner investigates. Key design points: 1) Entropy metric is computed serverside in the rollout plane with configurable dimensions and bucketing to avoid PII; 2) Exposure policy ties entropy, SLO violations, and cost burn rate into a small state machine (Normal -> Throttle -> Hold -> RehearseShadow); 3) RehearseShadow mode automatically mirrors a configurable percent of traffic to a shadow simulation that runs cheaper quantized variants and compares delta distributions; 4) Explainable fallback routes a small fraction of requests to a distilled rule-based scorer or simplified model that includes provenance metadata; 5) All signals are emitted to the Console: entropy_histogram, exposure_level, cost_burn_rate, fallback_activations. Rollout plan: This landed behind a feature flag rollout.entropy_canary; initial rollout to internal tenants only, then to beta orgs after one week of telemetry. Testing: Unit tests for entropy math and state transitions, integration test that simulates cohort collapse and verifies automatic hold and fallback activation. Also includes a small load test verifying scheduler respects throttle targets. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior is off; controllers without the flag retain current behavior. Observability & playbook: Added Console panels and a runbook describing how to interpret entropy signals and remediate. Why different from prior work: Prior rollouts focused on scalar SLO gates. This introduces a diversity-first signal and an explainability safety-liner during automated holds to reduce user-facing regressions while teams inspect root cause.
